# Cicada core reference for agents

<!-- Generated by internal/agentguide from the manual and the binary's catalogs. Do not edit; run
CICADA_UPDATE_AGENT_FRONT_DOOR=1 go test ./cmd/cicada -run TestAgentFrontDoorIsCurrent -->

The quick start, the language, sound and JSON formats in brief, then one line
for every command, edit intent, diagnostic code and effect route of this
binary. `cicada agents reference` prints this page; `cicada agents` prints the
quick start alone.

## Quick start

Cicada turns a text score into audio. A command that takes `--json` prints one
JSON document on standard output, on success and on failure: decide from it and
the exit status (0 is success).

### The loop

1. Start: `cicada new demo` makes the project folder `demo` with a song in
   `main.cicada`. Run every other command inside `demo`.
2. Write: replace `main.cicada` with your score (next section).
3. Check: `cicada check --json main.cicada`. Go on when `valid` is true.
   `scores[0].revision` is what your next edit must send.
4. Render: `cicada render main.cicada -o mix.wav --loudness -14 --json`. Go on
   when `ok` and `loudness.target_met` are true.
5. Listen: `cicada audition main.cicada --json`.
6. Edit: put intents in `edit.json`, preview with
   `cicada apply main.cicada edit.json --json`, then add `--write`. Go on when
   `ok` and `written` are true; repeat from step 3.

Step 1 prints:

```text
demo/main.cicada
```

### The score

Eight bars, three tracks:

```cicada
cicada 2
tempo 120
key a minor

track drums drums {}
track bass acid { cutoff = 700Hz }
track keys piano { octave = 3 level = -8dB }

pattern beat drums {
  bd: X... .... X... ..x.
  sd: .... X... .... X...
  ch: x.x. x.x. x.x. x.xx
}
pattern line { 1 . 1 . 5, . 1 . 1 . 1 . 3 . 5, . }
pattern chords { [1 3 5] - - - - - - . [6, 1 3] - - - - - - . }

scene verse { drums = beat bass = line keys = chords }
scene drop { drums = stop bass = line keys = chords }
song { verse*4 drop*2 verse*2 }

fx ceiling limiter { ceiling = -1dBTP }
master { insert = ceiling }
```

- Start every score with `cicada 2`. Outside a project, a score without it is
  edition 1, and some edits are refused.
- `track <name> <voice> { settings }`. Voices include `drums`, `acid`, `piano`,
  `fm_bass` and `poly_keys`. Values carry units.
- A pattern is 1 to 64 steps and repeats; 16 steps fill one bar. `.` is a
  rest, `-` holds the note before it, `|` only groups steps.
- `1` to `7` are degrees of the key's scale; `'` raises one an octave and `,`
  lowers it; they sound in the track's `octave` (default 2). `a1` and `c#3`
  are absolute (C4 is MIDI 60). `[1 3 5]` is a chord, except on `acid`, which
  plays it as three fast notes.
- A drum pattern has one row per lane (`bd sd ch oh cp rs lt mt ht cb cy`), all
  the same length: `x` hit, `X` accent, `.` silence.
- A scene gives each track a pattern (`stop` silences it). `song` plays scenes
  in order: `verse*4` is four bars of `verse`.
- The last two lines are a master limiter. Keep them (mistake 1).

```json
{"schema": "cicada.check.v1", "valid": true, "scores": [
  {"file": "main.cicada", "valid": true,
   "revision": "310f3c57244d24e1cf9eaf3e7185a80ff284c8a83af140b3901552fc07a15e32"}]}
```

### Hearing the result

```json
{"schema": "cicada.render.v1", "ok": true,
 "loudness": {"target_lufs": -14, "target_met": true}}
```

```json
{"schema": "cicada.audition.v1", "score": {"written_key": "A minor"},
 "heard_key": [{"key": "A minor"}], "harmony_mismatches": 0, "tracks": [
  {"id": "drums", "masked": false},
  {"id": "bass", "masked": true, "level_vs_loudest_db": -27.9}]}
```

- Too quiet: `tracks[].masked` (buried in the mix), or `level_vs_loudest_db`
  far below 0: here the bass is 27.9 dB under the drums.
- Too bright or dull: `tracks[].centroid_hz`; higher is brighter.
- Silent: `tracks[].silent`, or a bar in `bars` whose `match` is `silent`.
- Out of key: `heard_key[0].key` differs from `score.written_key`, or
  `harmony_mismatches` counts bars whose `match` is `disagree`.
- Clipping: `target_met` includes a true peak at or below
  `true_peak_max_dbtp`. Without `--loudness`, `levels.clipped_count` must be 0.
- `--from <bar> --bars <n>` limits `render` and `audition` to some bars.

### The envelope

A batch is checked whole and written as one revision, or not at all:

```json
{"version": 1, "revision": "310f3c57244d24e1cf9eaf3e7185a80ff284c8a83af140b3901552fc07a15e32", "intents": [
  {"kind": "setparam", "entity": "param:bass.level", "value": "6dB"},
  {"kind": "setparam", "entity": "param:drums.level", "value": "-10dB"},
  {"kind": "replacedeclaration", "declaration": "pattern", "name": "line",
   "text": "pattern line { 1 . 1 . 5, . 1 . 1 . 3 . 5 . 1' . }"}
]}
```

```json
{"schema": "cicada.apply.v1", "ok": true, "written": true,
 "revision_after": "157ddfb89b2ad22a8ce78f68ca2e0a8d65881efeb189390352474943261b9c2c"}
```

- `revision` is the SHA-256 of the score file in hex. Always send it: apply
  refuses (`revision_mismatch`) if the file changed since.
- Without `--write`, apply writes nothing and returns the `diff`.
- `entity` names what an intent changes: `param:<track>.<control>`,
  `pattern:<name>`, `step:<pattern>/<index>` (from 0), or on drums
  `step:<pattern>/<lane>/<index>`.
- When no intent fits, `replacedeclaration` replaces one declaration
  (`declaration` is `pattern`, `track_decl`, `scene_decl` or `song_decl`) and
  `replacetext` the whole score (`source`).

### Reading a refusal

A refusal exits non-zero; `apply` and `render` give `error` with a stable
`code` (branch on it) and a `message`.

- `check`: each of `scores[].diagnostics` has `code`, `message`,
  `start.line`, `start.column`, often a `hint`, and sometimes a `fix` whose
  `intents` you apply with `fix.revision`.
- `apply`: `error.code` is <!-- apply-error-codes -->`intent_refused`,
  `invalid_result` (the result does not check), `revision_mismatch`, `decode`,
  `read`, `write` or `usage`<!-- /apply-error-codes -->. `error.index` (from
  0), `error.kind` and, when known, `error.field` name the intent at fault, and
  `error.reason` a stable code for why. Nothing is written; resend the batch.
- `render`: `error.code` names the cause. A missed target still writes its
  best try, and `loudness.integrated_lufs` and `true_peak_dbtp` say what it
  reached: with no `remedy`, aim there or lower.

### Three mistakes to avoid

1. A loudness target with no master limiter: the song `cicada new` writes
   fails at -14 LUFS with `loudness_shortfall_at_true_peak_ceiling`. Way out:
   apply `error.remedy.intents` (the limiter) with `remedy.revision` and
   `--write`, then render again. The project then fails
   `check --profile browser`, as a browser image cannot carry a master insert
   yet; for the browser, keep the target at or below the error's
   `loudness.integrated_lufs`.
2. Reusing a revision after a write: `revision_mismatch`. Way out: send
   `revision_after` from the last apply, or run `check --json` again.
3. Guessing a name or a control: `apply` exits 1 with `intent_refused` and a
   message such as `unknown pattern "lines"` (`field` is `entity`) or
   `track keys does not expose sound parameter "cutoff"`. Way out: names from
   `symbols --json`. For a control, take a `path` from `cicada params` whose
   `voices` hold the track's engine (`fm_bass` is `fm`, `poly_keys` is
   `analog`, others their own name) and confirm it with `cicada explain`,
   which fails for a control the track lacks. `level` and `pan` fit any track.

### Look things up

- `cicada intents --json --index`: every kind and its meaning.
- `cicada intents --json <kind>`: a kind's fields and examples.
- `cicada symbols --json <score>`: the names a score defines.
- `cicada explain <score> <track>.<control>`: a control's value.
- `cicada params`: controls, with engine, unit and range.
- `cicada diagnostics --json <code>`: a code's meaning and fix.
- `cicada help --json <command>`: a command's usage and flags.

## Language

### Tracks and patterns

A track chooses a sound source: a built-in voice, a declared mono or poly
instrument, or an authored drum kit. The built-in voices are `drums`, the grand
`piano`, the 21 [keyboard patches](keys.md) such as `fm_bass` and `poly_keys`,
the [modeled percussion](modeled-percussion.md) instruments, and `acid`. A
pattern describes steps for that source. The scene connects a pattern to a
track by name.

The default grid uses sixteenth-note steps. A 16-step pattern fills one bar;
`step = 1/8`, `step = 1/4`, or an exact triplet division changes its resolution.
Patterns may contain 1–64 expanded steps and repeat while their scene plays. `.` is a
rest. `|` groups cells for your eyes and does not add a step.

The supported key scales are `minor`, `major`, `dorian`, `phrygian`,
`harmonic`, `pent`, `mixo`, and `blues`. Numbered pitches `1` through `7`
follow the selected scale. Letter pitches such as `c#3` name an absolute
pitch. Unnumbered letter pitches use the instrument's home octave, which
defaults to 2. MIDI note C4 is 60. An apostrophe raises a pitch an octave; a
comma lowers it. Leave a space between a letter pitch and a tie or next pitch:
write `c3 - e3`, not `c3-e3`.

Pattern settings go inside the braces before the steps. `swing` ranges from
50% to 75% and defaults to 50%; `gate` ranges from 10% to 100% and defaults
to 55%. `transpose` changes note patterns by −24 to +24 semitones. A pattern
without its own `seed` inherits the project seed. The project defaults are
130 BPM, A minor, and seed 0.

### Shape a note

Keep modifiers next to the note they change:

- `^` adds an accent on an `acid` track. Other voices ignore it; give them a
  `velocity:` row to vary their loudness.
- `~` slides into the next playable note. `acid`, authored synths and the
  guitar glide to the new pitch; the piano and the keyboard patches hold the
  first note until the next one starts.
- `*2` through `*8` retriggers the note that many times in one step.
- `?70` gives the note a 70% chance on each seeded pass.
- `-` ties the preceding note; `.` is a rest.

A note without `?` has a 100% chance. The legacy `%70` spelling is still
accepted; `cicada fix` changes it to `?70`.

Chance uses the pattern seed, track index, compiled pattern slot, pass number,
and step index. The same score therefore makes the same decisions in playback
and WAV export, independent of audio block size. All lanes of a drum pattern
use its compiled slot; a lane number does not replace the slot in the chance
hash. Changing a pattern's slot can change its seeded decisions.

You can reuse a phrase and transpose a use:

```cicada
cicada 2
track bass fm_bass {}
phrase hook { 1 . 1 5 }

pattern verse {
  use hook
  use hook +7
}

scene main { bass = verse }
song { main*8 }
```

Phrase uses expand before scheduling. Each use can repeat 1–64 times and
transpose by up to 24 semitones; the expanded pattern still has to fit the
64-step limit.

### Write drum rows

Each drum row names one of the built-in lanes. `x` is a hit at velocity 100,
`X` is an accented hit at velocity 127, and `x1`–`x9` select stepped
velocities. `.` leaves a cell silent. Rows in one pattern must have equal
length; any lane you leave out is silent.

The built-in lanes are `bd`, `sd`, `ch`, `oh`, `cp`, `rs`, `lt`, `mt`, `ht`,
`cb`, and `cy`. An authored kit can route a lane to a custom instrument or to
its built-in recipe. See the [kit and lane reference](../spec/edition-1.md#authored-kits).

## Sound

### Score master effects

A score can declare each processor and order it on the master. Native playback,
WAV export, and stems export prepare these effects before audio rendering.
Studio shows the saved chain, followed by the built-in safety limiter.

```cicada
cicada 2
track bass fm_bass {}
pattern pulse { 1 . 3 . 5 . 3 . }
scene main { bass = pulse }
song { main*16 }
fx tone eq { type = highpass frequency = 25Hz q = 0.707 }
fx glue comp { threshold = -18dB ratio = 2 makeup = 1dB }
fx punch transient { attack = 2dB sustain = -1dB }
fx stereo width { amount = 1.08 bass_mono = 100Hz }
fx ceiling limiter { ceiling = -1dBTP lookahead = 3ms release = 100ms }
master { insert = tone -> glue -> punch -> stereo -> ceiling }
export broadcast { loudness = -23LUFS true_peak = -1dBTP normalize = off }
```

Run `cicada render score.cicada --export broadcast --bars 16 -o broadcast.wav`.
The export target uses the existing iterative BS.1770 loudness renderer and
measures the delivered WAV. Live playback does not apply programme normalization.
An unreachable target returns an error instead of claiming success. This
one-track bass cannot reach a −14 LUFS streaming target, because the renderer
adds at most 12 dB of input gain, so the example asks for the −23 LUFS
broadcast level.

#### Export loudness targets

A loudness target (`--loudness`, or an `export` block with `loudness`) renders
the score in up to six passes. Each pass measures the delivered WAV and adjusts
one static gain. Where that gain goes depends on the master chain.

| Master chain | Where the gain goes | What holds the true-peak ceiling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No limiter | Direct renderer: after the master chain. Scheduled renderer (arrangements, audio clips, serial track effects, sample packs): at the master input, as in earlier releases, because the engine applies its master gain before the chain. Output is unchanged from earlier releases. | The gain stops at the ceiling. It keeps crest factor, so an ambitious target can miss and returns a shortfall error. |
| Contains a `limiter` | At the master input: after the music and SFX buses sum and the master `level`, before the chain. | Your limiter. The extra level reaches it, so it reduces peaks and a punchy mix can get louder than its natural crest allows. |

Without a limiter, a target that the render misses at the true-peak ceiling
ends its error with the fix: add a limiter at the export's true-peak ceiling
as the last master insert, such as `fx ceiling limiter { ceiling = -1dBTP }`
with `master { insert = ceiling }`. `cicada render --json` reports it as the
code `loudness_shortfall_at_true_peak_ceiling` with a `remedy` that holds the
exact score text for that score and ceiling, and the `addeffect` intent that
makes the same change with `cicada apply`
([agent formats](agents.md#render---json)).

With a limiter in the chain, the renderer keeps two guard rails:

- Input gain is capped at +12 dB.
- The chain limiter's gain reduction is held to 6 dB or less. Ordinary
  streaming masters use a few dB of limiting; 6 dB is the upper end.

A target that needs more than either limit stops short and returns a shortfall
error that names the limit that bound. The WAV from the best pass is still
written (Studio keeps it as a separate shortfall file). When even a render
that breaks a limit is too quiet for the target, and the best render is within
0.5 dB of the reduction maximum, the search stops instead of using all six
passes. The render summary reports the applied gain, the gain stage (`master_input` when the gain runs ahead of the master chain, `post_chain` when it runs after it or there is no chain), the
chain limiter's largest gain reduction, and the largest gain reduction of any
limiter. Review these numbers and run `cicada verify-wav` on the result.

Only the first pass synthesizes the mix, on both renderers and with or without
a master chain. It stores the signal that enters the master stage (the summed
buses, before the master `level` and the export gain) in a temporary file next
to the output, and later passes play that signal back through the master
gain, the chain and the safety limiter with the new gain. A pass whose gain
differs from an earlier pass's by less than the renderer's gain can show is not
rendered at all: it reuses that pass's audio and measurement. The result
matches rendering every pass in full, byte for byte. The render summary counts
the full syntheses, the cached replays and the repeated passes, and lists each
pass's gain, loudness and true peak. `CICADA_RENDER_NO_REUSE=1` turns the reuse
off, so every pass synthesizes the song (see the [CLI reference](../cli.md)).

The file takes about 23 MB per minute at 48 kHz, counted from the start of the
song to the end of the exported range plus its tail, so an export of the last
bars of a long song stores the whole song up to them. It stays until the export
ends, on the same disk as the export's two other temporary WAV files (one holds
the pass being rendered, the other the best pass so far). On a nearly full disk
it can take space that those files need, so the export frees it as follows:

- If the export cannot create the file, or a write to it fails, it renders every
  pass in full.
- If a pass, or the copy of a pass to the best-pass file, fails while the file
  exists, the export deletes the file, repeats that step without it, and renders
  every later pass in full. A pass fails when its render, its sync to disk or its
  close fails, or when the stored signal cannot be read back.
- If the repeated step fails too, the export stops with that error.

Passes rendered without the file take longer, but the WAV and the report are the
same.

The same renderer serves `cicada render --export`, `--loudness`, and Studio's
export. `cicada stems` does not apply loudness targets. The built-in safety
limiter (ceiling -0.3 dBFS) still follows the chain in both modes.

| Kind | Controls (defaults; ranges) |
| --- | --- |
| `eq` | `type = peak` (`peak`, `low_shelf`, `high_shelf`, `highpass`, `lowpass`); `frequency = 1000Hz` (10 Hz to 0.45 × render rate); `q = 1` (0.1–20); `gain = 0dB` (−24 to +24 dB). Declare separate EQ effects for multiple bands. |
| `comp` | Existing compressor controls: `threshold`, `ratio`, `knee`, `attack`, `release`, `makeup`, `detect`, `mix`. Master compression detects its own stereo input. |
| `transient` | `attack = 0dB`, `sustain = 0dB` (−18 to +18 dB); `fast = 1ms` (0.1–10 ms), `slow = 30ms` (10–100 ms, greater than fast), `release = 120ms` (20–1000 ms). |
| `width` | `amount = 1` (0–2); `bass_mono = 0Hz` (bypass, or 20–500 Hz). |
| `limiter` | `ceiling = -1dBTP` (−12 to 0 dBTP); `lookahead = 3ms` (1–10 ms); `release = 100ms` (20–1000 ms). |
| `convolution` | Required `asset` name; `mix = 0.15` (0–1); `partition = 128frames` (power of two, 64–2048). See [score impulses](../audio/convolution.md#score-impulses). |

The chain accepts at most 16 distinct effect names, in any order. Processing and
reset allocate no memory. Offline export removes the summed processor latency
and drains delayed final samples. Omission or `insert = none` preserves legacy
output. Tracks accept eight serial inserts; the music bus still accepts one compressor. Master effects have
fixed controls until recompilation; scene settings and live parameter paths for
them are rejected. A compressor cannot share state between music and master.

Prepared processors cannot be encoded into a core WASM project image. Browser
score playback needs the companion modules connected by its host; that wiring
is separate from native playback and Studio's saved-chain display. The master companion remains separate from core track processing.

### JSON schema

`--json` prints one object. Field names are stable within the `format` value
`cicada.audition/1`. Decibel values are rounded to 0.1, other numbers to 2 or 3
decimals. Levels below the floor read -120.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | string | Always `cicada.audition.v1`, named as the other `--json` formats are ([agent formats](agents.md)). |
| `format` | string | Always `cicada.audition/1`. |
| `title` | string | Score title. |
| `sample_rate` | number | Render rate in Hz (48000). |
| `score.tempo_bpm` | number | Score tempo. |
| `score.written_key` | string | Key from the score, for example `A minor`. |
| `score.song_bars` | number | Bars in the whole song. |
| `score.from_bar`, `score.bars` | number | First analyzed bar (one-based) and the count. |
| `score.tempo_changes[]` | array | Scene tempo steps that govern the analyzed bars: `bar` (one-based) and `bpm`. Omitted when none. `score.tempo_bpm` stays the score tempo. |
| `score.swing[]` | array | One entry per distinct swing value, ascending: `swing_percent`, `tracks`, `patterns`. Omitted when none. |
| `heard_key[]` | array | Top three keys from the summed pitched stems: `key` (for example `C major`), `score` (correlation). |
| `full_mix_key[]` | array | The same from the whole mix. |
| `audibility_db` | number | Pitched stems against the whole mix, 125 Hz to 2 kHz, in dB. |
| `masked_bars` | number | Bars with `masked` true. |
| `bars[]` | array | One per analyzed bar: `bar` (one-based), `written_notes` (pitch classes), `written`, `heard` (from the pitched stems), `heard_fit` (0..1 cosine similarity of the pitch-class energy to the chosen chord), `mix_rms_dbfs`, `audibility_db`, `masked` (`audibility_db` below -15), `match` (`agree`, `disagree`, `no-written-pitch`, `silent`). |
| `harmony_mismatches` | number | Count of bars with `match` `disagree`. |
| `tracks[]` | array | One per track, in score order: `id`, `silent` (true under -80 dBFS; the other fields except `rms_dbfs` are then zero, including `energy_share_pct`, and the silent track is left out of the other tracks' shares), `rms_dbfs`, `level_vs_loudest_db`, `energy_share_pct`, `band_vs_mix_db`, `masked` (`band_vs_mix_db` below -15), `centroid_hz`, `attack_ms`, `decay20_ms`, `decay20_lower_bound`, `onsets`, `active_bars` (bars where the track plays or sounds), `onsets_per_bar`, `swing_percent`, `rhythm` (16 numbers, 0..1, slot 1 first). |
| `sections[]` | array | `name`, `tempo_bpm` (tempo at the section start), `from_bar` (bar holding the first tick, one-based), `to_bar` (bar holding the last tick, inclusive), `from_tick`, `to_tick` (absolute ticks, end exclusive), `rms_dbfs`, `centroid_hz`, `onsets_per_bar`, `tracks`. |
| `images[]` | array | File names written to `-o`. Omitted without `-o`. |

## Formats

An agent can run the whole loop from the command line and read every result as
JSON: discover the commands, learn the edit intents, check a score, edit it,
render it to a loudness target and listen to it. This page describes each JSON
format, with an example that the binary produced.

The `--json` formats share these rules:

- Every run with `--json` prints exactly one JSON document on standard output,
  on success and on every failure, a usage error included. Warnings,
  diagnostics as text and error messages go to standard error.
- Every document has a `schema` field that names its format and version, in
  the form `cicada.<format>.v<version>`, such as `cicada.check.v1`. A field is
  added in a compatible way; a change that would break a reader gets a new
  version. `cicada audition --json` also keeps its older `format` field
  (`cicada.audition/1`) beside `schema` (`cicada.audition.v1`).
- Keys are snake_case. Lists whose order has no meaning are sorted, and no
  document carries a timestamp. The one older format outside these rules is
  `cicada symbols --json`: a list of symbols without a schema, whose positions
  use the keys `Line` and `Column`.
- Paths follow one rule in every document: a path inside the working folder is
  relative to it, with forward slashes (`sub/song.cicada`); a path outside it
  is absolute.
- A failure carries an `error` object with a stable `code` and the `message`
  the command prints. `check` also reports `valid` false, and its diagnostics.
- The exit status is the same as without `--json`:

  | Command | Success | Failure | Usage error or unknown name |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `check`, `apply`, `intents`, `diagnostics`, `audition` | 0 | 1 | 1 |
  | `render`, `stems` | 0 | 1 | 2 |
  | `help`, `agents` | 0 | — | 2 |

Usage errors and unknown names have the codes `usage`, `unknown_kind`
(`intents`), `unknown_code` (`diagnostics`) and `unknown_command` (`help`).

`cicada audition --json` is described in [Audition](audition.md), and
`cicada verify-wav --report` in [Exporting](exporting.md). The loudness fields
use the names of `verify-wav --report` (`integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`,
`clipped_count`); Studio's export report calls the integrated loudness
`achieved_lufs`.

### Error codes of apply --json

- `usage`: the arguments are wrong.
- `read`: the score or the intents file cannot be read.
- `decode`: the JSON does not match the envelope or an intent's kind.
- `revision_mismatch`: the envelope's `revision` is not the score's.
- `intent_refused`: an intent is refused.
- `invalid_result`: the edited score does not compile.
- `write`: the edit could not be written.

### Error codes of render --json

- `usage`: the arguments are wrong.
- `unreadable_score`: the score cannot be read.
- `invalid_score`: the score has errors; `diagnostics` lists them.
- `export_settings`: the `--export` profile is unknown or cannot be applied.
- `output_exists`: the stems folder already exists.
- `sampler_memory`: the sampler packs exceed the resident PCM cap.
- `render_failed`: another render or write error; the message says which.
- `true_peak_and_dc_unmet`: no pass met the true-peak ceiling and the DC limit.
- `loudness_unmeasurable`: the render has no measurable loudness.
- `true_peak_over_ceiling`: the best pass is still above the true-peak ceiling.
- `limiter_reduction_over_maximum`: the master limiter would reduce more than 6 dB.
- `loudness_shortfall_at_limiter_maximum`: the target needs more than the master limiter's 6 dB maximum.
- `loudness_shortfall_at_input_gain_cap`: the target needs more than +12 dB ahead of the master limiter.
- `loudness_shortfall_at_true_peak_ceiling`: without a master limiter, the gain stops at the true-peak ceiling.
- `loudness_target_missed`: the best pass is outside the tolerance for another reason.

## Commands

- `cicada new`: create an edition-2 project
- `cicada agents`: print the quick start for AI agents
- `cicada bundle`: package a portable score with provenance
- `cicada apply`: apply typed edit intents to a score
- `cicada intents`: list the edit intents apply accepts
- `cicada diagnostics`: list the diagnostic codes with their meaning and fix
- `cicada fix`: migrate legacy source spellings
- `cicada check`: validate one score or the current project
- `cicada fmt`: format a score or current project
- `cicada play`: play and watch a score
- `cicada studio`: open the local workstation
- `cicada lsp`: run the editor language server
- `cicada fields`: print the project field catalog as JSON
- `cicada params`: print the parameter catalog as JSON
- `cicada view`: write a score or project view as HTML
- `cicada explain`: explain a language item or parameter value
- `cicada gen`: generate a deterministic phrase
- `cicada convert`: convert source and semantic JSON
- `cicada compare`: compare two projects
- `cicada highlight`: print source with syntax highlighting
- `cicada symbols`: list source definitions and references
- `cicada render`: render a score to WAV
- `cicada stems`: render separate float32 WAV stems
- `cicada audition`: report what a score sounds like
- `cicada verify-wav`: verify WAV samples and timing
- `cicada verify-stems`: verify a stem directory
- `cicada wam2`: export a WAM2 instrument
- `cicada director`: write the Game Director manifest for browser hosts
- `cicada game-score`: compile a score into a score pack for a GoSX game
- `cicada midi`: export a Standard MIDI File
- `cicada verify-midi`: verify a Standard MIDI File
- `cicada compare-midi`: compare MIDI event streams
- `cicada import-midi`: import MIDI notes as a score
- `cicada golden`: check the reference render fingerprint
- `cicada validate`: validate one score
- `cicada ast`: print the typed syntax tree as JSON
- `cicada events`: print events for one pattern
- `cicada graph`: print one compiled instrument graph
- `cicada transcribe`: transcribe a sung, hummed or solo-instrument WAV into score rows
- `cicada fit-model`: fit a recorded hit to a playable modal instrument
- `cicada record-kit`: build one drum-kit sampler pack from your own recorded takes
- `cicada record-pack`: slice user WAV recordings into a pinned sampler pack
- `cicada lib`: manage pinned source and audio libraries
- `cicada lib list`: list available std, project, and user libraries
- `cicada lib show`: inspect a resolved library
- `cicada lib new`: scaffold an edition-2 library
- `cicada lib update`: pin imported library content
- `cicada lib vendor`: copy imported user libraries into project lib/
- `cicada save-as`: copy a score, audio, and pinned libraries

## Edit intents

`cicada intents --json <kind>` gives a kind's fields and examples.

- `addaudiotrack`: declares a new, empty audio track in an edition-2 score
- `addeffect`: declares a new effect and, with InsertOn, inserts it in one edit
- `addmarker`: appends a marker at the end of the arrange block
- `addmodulator`: appends one modulation source: an LFO, a sway, a contour or an envelope follower
- `addplacement`: appends a placement at the end of the arrange block
- `addpreset`: inserts an authored instrument and its track in one edit
- `appendsongentry`: adds an entry at the end of the song block
- `bindperformedgroup`: binds one note of a performance pattern to a shared gesture lane, or unbinds it
- `bindscene`: makes a scene play a pattern on a track, replacing what the scene played there before
- `convertsongtoarrange`: rewrites a `song` block as an `arrange` block of placements
- `copyplacement`: appends a copy of a placement under a new name; settings override the copied fields
- `createpattern`: creates a grid for a track's instrument
- `cyclestep`: moves the ratchet or the chance of one note step to its next value
- `deleteclip`: removes a placement and the comment lines attached above it
- `deletesongentry`: removes one entry of the song block
- `duplicateclip`: places a copy of a placement directly after the original
- `duplicatepattern`: copies a pattern under a new name
- `duplicatesongentry`: inserts a copy of one song entry right after it
- `editmodulator`: changes one setting or one contour point in its owning file, or removes a source that no route uses
- `editnotes`: moves, resizes, changes the velocity of, deletes, inserts or quantizes a batch of notes in one pattern as one edit
- `insertlibraryitem`: imports a library and binds a track to one of its items
- `modulationroute`: adds, changes the depth of, or removes one identified route
- `moveclip`: moves a placement to a new start tick
- `movesongentry`: moves one entry of the song block to another position
- `placesamplerprint`: declares a printed sampler performance as an asset and a clip, and places it on an audio track in the arrange block
- `placevocalcomp`: writes a printed vocal comp into the score: an asset, a clip and a placement on the track, between `cicada-vocal-begin` and `cicada-vocal-end` comments
- `publishrecorded`: adds the sampler, track, pattern and scene binding for a recording pack
- `recordtake`: commits all recorded patterns as one validated edit
- `removearrangementtempo`: removes the tempo step at one position of the arrange block
- `removeautomationpoint`: removes the point at At (or at OldAt when given) and removes the lane when it was the lane's last point
- `removeeffect`: deletes an effect: its declaration, the comment lines above it and a comment after it on its line, and the routes that carry it (its place in track, music and master insert chains, and track sends to it)
- `removemarker`: removes the declaration of one marker
- `removeplacement`: removes the declaration of one placement and nothing else
- `removescenesetting`: removes one parameter setting from a scene
- `replacedeclaration`: replaces one declaration's syntax span
- `replacetext`: saves a complete buffer verbatim, after Apply validates it
- `resizeclip`: sets a placement length
- `resizepattern`: changes a pattern's length in steps, adding rests at the end or removing the last steps
- `resizeperformance`: changes the loop length of a performance pattern
- `savepreset`: appends the declaration prepared by the host, including any direct import or snapshot of a private library instrument
- `scaleperformance`: changes musical timing while keeping pitches and controls
- `selecttake`: makes a scene play one recorded take on an audio track
- `setarrangementtempo`: adds a bar-boundary tempo step
- `setautomationpoint`: adds or edits one point of a parameter's automation lane (an `automate <path> { ..
- `setchord`: places a voicing and its hold steps as one reversible edit
- `setclipsettings`: sets an audio clip's source region, gain and fades together
- `setdrumvelocity`: sets the velocity of one drum hit, written as the nearest hit spelling (x, x1 to x9 or X)
- `setmarker`: moves one marker
- `setmidimapping`: writes one learned input to the score's logical port
- `setparam`: sets or resets one parameter
- `setpatternsettings`: changes a pattern's swing, gate and transpose without changing its note text
- `setperformancegroup`: adds, renames or removes one shared gesture lane of a performance pattern
- `setperformedexpression`: edits one note-owned controller sample
- `setperformednote`: edits, adds or removes one note of a performance pattern
- `setpitch`: sets the pitch of one note step, or adds or removes that pitch in a chord step
- `setprojectsettings`: sets the score's title, tempo, key root and scale together
- `setrange`: clears, copies, reverses, rotates or transposes a range of steps in one pattern lane
- `setscenesetting`: sets the value a parameter takes when a scene starts, or adds that setting to the scene
- `setsharedexpression`: edits, adds or removes one point of a shared gesture lane
- `setsongbars`: sets how many bars one song entry plays its scene
- `setsongscene`: changes the scene one song entry plays
- `setstep`: writes one step: a note, a drum hit, a tie or a rest
- `shapeperformancepitch`: changes note pitches while retaining their articulation
- `splitclip`: cuts a placement in two at a pattern-length boundary
- `togglemodifier`: turns the accent or the slide of one note step on or off
- `togglestep`: turns one grid step on or off: a rest becomes a note (1, or x on a drum lane) and anything else becomes a rest
- `updateplacement`: patches the named fields of one placement in place
- `varyplacement`: copies a placement's compiled pattern into the entry score and changes only that placement to use it

## Diagnostic codes

`cicada diagnostics --json <code>` gives a code's fix.

- `CICADA-ARRANGEMENT` (error): an arrange block is invalid: it is used together with a song block or in an edition-1 score; it has no placements; a placement or marker has an unknown field, lacks at (or a placement its length), has a malformed or out-of-range time, or a time whose source and typed values differ; a placement's ID is invalid, its content has no track slot, its pattern does not suit its track, or a step pattern placement starts between steps
- `CICADA-ASSET-FORMAT` (error): an audio asset's declared format, frames, rate or channels are invalid or differ from the WAV file
- `CICADA-ASSET-HASH` (error): an audio asset's sha256 is malformed or does not match the file's bytes
- `CICADA-ASSET-MISSING` (error): an audio asset's file, or the project or library folder it lives in, cannot be read
- `CICADA-ASSET-PATH` (error): an audio asset's path leaves the project folder, or a library asset is not under audio/
- `CICADA-AUDIO` (error): browser audio is not ready for the request: transport stopped, worklet send failed, or a reset is pending
- `CICADA-CAPABILITY` (error): the public demo session does not offer this command
- `CICADA-CHAIN` (error): a track's chain names no patterns or more than 32
- `CICADA-CLIP-RANGE` (error): an audio clip's region, gain or fades are invalid, or a clip is bound to a track that is not an audio track
- `CICADA-DEMO` (error): the public demo host refused its build or request (missing source commit, unsupported host, bad asset or entry document)
- `CICADA-DIRECTOR` (error): the live block cannot become a Game Director manifest: an invalid state or stinger name, or a stinger pattern without a track slot
- `CICADA-DUPLICATE` (error): a name is declared twice in one namespace, or uses a reserved name; the message names the first declaration
- `CICADA-EXPANSION` (error): a pattern expands beyond 64 steps after its phrase uses
- `CICADA-EXPERIMENTAL` (error): an experimental voice (guitar) is used without opting in
- `CICADA-GRID` (error): a step grid attribute or tuplet group is invalid: tuplets need 2 to 8 pitches that divide a cell into whole ticks of at least 30
- `CICADA-HISTORY` (error): the public demo session has no change to undo or redo
- `CICADA-IO` (error): a file cannot be read, or has an extension the command does not accept
- `CICADA-KEY` (error): the key root or scale is unknown
- `CICADA-LIB-ASSET` (error): convert cannot write library-owned audio into semantic JSON
- `CICADA-LIB-CAPABILITY` (error): an imported library requires an engine edition or capability this cicada does not support
- `CICADA-LIB-CYCLE` (error): libraries import each other in a cycle
- `CICADA-LIB-DECL` (error): a library declares something only a score may declare, or a qualified name
- `CICADA-LIB-HASH` (error): an imported library is not pinned in cicada.sum, or its content differs from the pin
- `CICADA-LIB-IMPORT` (error): a score with imports was parsed without the project source loader
- `CICADA-LIB-MISSING` (error): an imported library is not found in std, the project lib/ folder or the user library
- `CICADA-LIB-PATH` (error): a library path is invalid, or names std where a user library is required
- `CICADA-LIB-PRIVATE` (error): a score references a library declaration that is private
- `CICADA-LIB-REFERENCE` (error): a library reference does not name a declaration, uses a namespace no import binds, or a library parameter path lacks a direct import
- `CICADA-LIB-ROOT` (error): scores in different folders keep separate library pins
- `CICADA-LIB-SHADOW` (error): an import namespace collides with a declaration, another import or the reserved builtin namespace, or a library exists in more than one search location
- `CICADA-LIB-SOURCE` (error): a library's source file cannot be read
- `CICADA-LIB-SUM` (error): cicada.sum is malformed
- `CICADA-LIMIT` (error): a size or count limit is exceeded: name length, steps, tracks, voices, graph nodes, chain stages, image size, held inputs or source size
- `CICADA-LIVE-ATTACK` (error): a live layers attack other than 1bar is given
- `CICADA-LIVE-BLOCK` (error): the live block is repeated, comes before a track, repeats a setting, or leaves an array implicit
- `CICADA-LIVE-COUNT-IN` (error): the live count_in is not 0 to 8 whole bars
- `CICADA-LIVE-LAND` (error): the live land value is unknown
- `CICADA-LIVE-LIMIT` (error): the live block has more than 16 macros, or layers use more than 3 distinct thresholds
- `CICADA-LIVE-MACRO` (error): a live macro is duplicated, badly named, out of range, or maps to an invalid target
- `CICADA-LIVE-PHRASE` (error): the live phrase is not 1 to 64 bars
- `CICADA-LIVE-RECORD` (error): the live record division does not resolve to 30 to 3840 ticks
- `CICADA-LIVE-RELEASE` (error): the live layers release is not 1 to 16 bars
- `CICADA-LIVE-TRACK` (error): a live layer rule names an unknown track or repeats one
- `CICADA-LOCKED` (error): a phrase repair would need to change a locked step
- `CICADA-MANIFEST` (error): cicada.mod has an unknown, repeated or malformed directive
- `CICADA-MIDI` (error): the midi block is invalid: a port is unknown or repeated, a channel is outside 1 to 16, a note or controller outside 0 to 127, or a mapping target is invalid
- `CICADA-NOTE` (error): a live note was refused: invalid input identity, note or velocity, or a voice without browser live notes
- `CICADA-NOTES` (error): an editnotes batch was refused because of one note; the reason and the note (at, step, pitch or lane) come as data
- `CICADA-PARAM` (error): a parameter, attribute or setting is unknown, out of range, or not allowed here
- `CICADA-PERFORMANCE` (error): a performance pattern is invalid: bad note fields, overlapping gates of one pitch, gesture times outside a note, or ticks outside a performance
- `CICADA-POSITION` (error): a position is invalid or out of order: arrangement tempo steps, automation points or contour points
- `CICADA-PRESET-PARAM` (error): a preset sets a parameter its target instrument does not have, or a structural one
- `CICADA-PRESET-RANGE` (error): a preset value is outside its parameter's range
- `CICADA-PRESET-TARGET` (error): a preset's instrument target is missing or incompatible
- `CICADA-PRESET-TYPE` (error): a preset value has the wrong type: not one of the allowed values, not on or off, not a finite number or not an integer
- `CICADA-PRESET-UNIT` (error): a preset value has the wrong unit
- `CICADA-RATE` (error, warning): a modulator's rate is not what it plays: the warning when loop = continue fits whole cycles to the song at another rate, the error when a routed modulator exceeds 20 Hz at the song's fastest tempo
- `CICADA-REFERENCE` (error): a name refers to nothing: an unknown track, pattern, scene, instrument, effect, bus, clip, asset or profile; close names get a spelling suggestion
- `CICADA-REVISION` (error): the public demo session changed since the client read it
- `CICADA-ROUTE` (error): a modulation route reaches a target it cannot modulate: a legacy effect setting, a non-track row, a non-continuous row, or an envelope's own input
- `CICADA-ROW` (error): a velocity row is invalid: wrong length, a value outside 1 to 127, or a holding dot with no earlier value
- `CICADA-SAMPLER-MEMORY` (error): the sampler packs decode to more PCM than the resident cap allows
- `CICADA-SAMPLER-PACK` (error): a sampler pack is declared wrongly or does not load at 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz
- `CICADA-SAMPLER-PARAM` (error): a sampler's fields are invalid: root, mode, voices, envelope or the field set
- `CICADA-SAMPLER-ZONE` (error, warning): a note falls outside every zone of its sampler pack, or a hit velocity no zone covers (errors); a warning when a hit's velocity is outside the recorded range and plays at the nearest recorded one
- `CICADA-SCALE-DEGREE` (error): a scale degree does not exist in the score's scale (2 and 6 in pent and blues)
- `CICADA-SEED` (error): a seed is outside 0 to 4294967295
- `CICADA-SLIDE-REST` (warning): a slide leads into a rest, so it has no effect
- `CICADA-SOLO` (warning): a saved solo switch is on, so render and check play only the soloed parts
- `CICADA-SOURCE-MISSING` (error): a score that cicada.mod lists cannot be read
- `CICADA-SOURCE-PATH` (error): a source path is absolute, uses traversal or patterns, is not listed in cicada.mod, or leaves the project
- `CICADA-SYNTAX` (error): the text does not parse: a token or declaration is malformed
- `CICADA-UNIT` (error): a value has the wrong unit or type for its field
- `CICADA-UNSUPPORTED` (error): valid notation that the engine does not implement: a route, effect kind or placement, a setting without an engine representation, or an export option combination
- `CICADA-USE` (error): a phrase use is invalid: repeat outside 1 to 64 or transpose outside -24 to 24
- `CICADA-VERSION` (error): the edition is unsupported, the score header and cicada.mod disagree, or a removed edition-1 spelling is used

## Effect routes

Where `addeffect` may put each kind. A send return takes no `inserton`;
raise `param:<track>.send.<name>` instead.

| Kind | Inserted on | Send return | Only in an insert chain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ampcab` | track | no | no |
| `chorus` | track | no | no |
| `comp` | track, music, master | no | yes |
| `convolution` | master | no | yes |
| `deesser` | track | no | no |
| `delay` | none | yes | no |
| `drive` | track | no | no |
| `eq` | track, master | no | no |
| `limiter` | master | no | yes |
| `reverb` | none | yes | no |
| `tape` | none | yes | no |
| `transient` | master | no | yes |
| `width` | master | no | yes |
